functions.name: DDSHeaderParsing
functions.summary: Parse a compact DDS-style header and then either expose the surface's first-row data or fully decode its pixels into the object's buffers. On the format-41 path it expands a 16/24/32-bit palette into a 1024-byte RGBA buffer at this+0x8 (owned via this+0x3C). It then either aliases the source buffer at this+0x4 (fast path, this+0x38 = 0) or allocates and decodes the full surface row-by-row into this+0x4 (this+0x38 = 1), honoring the orientation flags v40/v41 and the remaining-data budget v57. Returns 0 on success, -2147467259 on malformed or undersized input, -2147024882 on allocation failure.

Reject undersized input: if the buffer size a3 is below 18 (0x12) bytes, return -2147467259.
Header byte a2[1] (format/compression selector) must be 0 or 1; if (a2[1] & 0xFE) != 0 return -2147467259.
Header byte a2[2] must have all bits above bit 1 clear ((a2[2] & 0xFFFFFFF4) == 0) and the width (WORD at a2+12) and height (WORD at a2+14) must both be non-zero; otherwise return -2147467259.
Compute first-stage bytes-per-pixel v9 = (a2[7] + 7) >> 3 from the a2[7] bit-depth byte; used for the first-row size.
Map the first-stage bit depth a2[7] to the internal format code v46: 15 -> 24, 16 -> 25, 24 -> 20, 32 -> 21; any other value returns -2147467259.
Compute second-stage bytes-per-pixel v50 = (a2[16] + 7) >> 3 from the a2[16] bit-depth byte; used as the block copy unit for the surface data.

Map (a2[2] & 3) to the surface format code v49: 1 -> 41 (requires a2[1] == 0 and a2[16] == 8), 2 -> the same 20/21/24/25 mapping applied to a2[16], 3 -> 50 (requires a2[16] == 8); any violating combination returns -2147467259.
Capture orientation flags from header byte a2[17]: v40 = (a2[17] & 0x20) == 0x20, v41 = (a2[17] & 0x10) != 0x10, and v39 = a2[2] & 8 (zero given the earlier guard).
Locate the payload: v17 = a2[0] (sub-header size), v55 = a3 - 18; if v55 < v17 return -2147467259; remaining size v56 = v55 - v17 and surface data pointer v51 = a2 + v17 + 18.
Compute the first-row size v36 = v9 * (WORD at a2+5); if v56 < v36 return -2147467259 because the buffer cannot hold even the first row.
The palette decode path runs only when the request flag this+0x40 is set and the resolved format v49 == 41.
Palette dimensions (WORD at a2+3 plus WORD at a2+5) must not exceed 256 entries; otherwise return -2147467259.
Allocate a 1024-byte palette buffer via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and store it at this+0x8; a null allocation returns -2147024882.
Mark the palette buffer as owned: this+0x3C = 1, then initialize the whole 0x400-byte palette to 0xFF via memset.

Convert each palette entry from the v46 source format (20 = 24-bit BGR, 21 = 32-bit BGRA, 24 = RGB565 expand, 25 = RGB555 expand) to a 4-byte RGBA pixel (R at +0, G at +1, B at +2, A at +3), writing into this+0x8 until the destination pointer reaches 4 * (palette width + palette height).
After palette handling, derive the remaining size v57 = v56 - v36, the next-row pointer v28 = v51 + v36, and the full surface byte size v29 = v50 * width * height.

Store the decoded header fields: format code v49 at this+0x0; first-row data pointer (v51 + v36) at this+0x4; row stride v50 * width at this+0x30; 0 at this+0x34; width at this+0xC; height at this+0x10; literal 1 at this+0x14.
If the request flag this+0x40 == 0, only the header was requested: return 0 without decoding any surface data (guard:0).

Fast path: when v39 == 0 and v40 and v41 and the remaining data v57 covers the full surface size v29, point this+0x4 directly at the source-buffer position v28 (no allocation), clear the ownership flag this+0x38 = 0, and return 0.
Otherwise allocate v29 bytes via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper for the surface data, store the result at this+0x4, return -2147024882 if the allocation fails, and mark ownership this+0x38 = 1.

Per-row surface copy: for each of the height rows, copy v50-byte blocks from the source into the row destination v54, honoring the remaining-size budget v57 and returning -2147467259 when v57 < v50 mid-row; v41 controls the block direction along the row and v40 controls the row-to-row advance by +/- stride. functions.name: InitializeMediaSurfaceFromStream
functions.summary: Initializes a media-surface context from a binary stream: validates the input with a bounded compare, creates a versioned subsystem ("1.0.5") plus a calloc-like working buffer under a setjmp error frame, parses format metadata (dimensions, pixel depth, format identifier) that maps to a codec identifier, upgrades it to FOURCC-style literals for the 16-bpp case, negotiates a mode selector and row stride, allocates the pixel-data buffer and row-pointer table, and for the paletted format builds a 256-entry RGBA colour-conversion table with optional gamma correction.

Allocate the working parse buffer: v56 = CallocLikeAllocator(v3); on failure jump to the cleanup path

Process the parsed data into the working buffer: sub_5119E9(v57, v56)
Read format metadata: sub_5121AE(v57, v56, &v46, &v52, &v49, &v47, 0, 0, 0) yields width v46, height v52, pixel depth v49, and format identifier v47

Optional scalar setting: if FlagGuardedByteReader(v57, v56, &v44) succeeds call FlagSetterWithGuard_3b36(v57, v56, v44); otherwise GuardedFloatToDoubleConversion reads a double into v41 and CameraRotationStateSetter(v57, 2.2, v41[0]) is invoked
Codec upgrade: if this[0] != 41 and MaskedReadAt8(v57, v56, 16) succeeds, call sub_5124D5 and upgrade this[0]: 20 -> 21, 50 -> 51, 909200416 -> 909200449, 909201952 -> 909201985

Finalize RGB: if this[0] == 20, call StateFlagSetter_2366(v57, 255, 1) and write 22 into this[0]

Commit dimensions and valid flag: this[3] = v46 (width), this[4] = v52 (height), this[5] = 1
Compute the row stride: v18 = ShortComputation_212e(v57, v56); this[12] = v18 and this[13] = 0
Allocation precondition: buffer/palette allocation proceeds only when this[16] (evaluated as this[16] == 0) is nonzero
Allocate the pixel-data buffer: v20 = OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(v52 * v18) stored at this[1]; on failure jump to cleanup; this[14] is set to 1
Allocate the row-pointer table: v51 = OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(4 * v52); on failure jump to cleanup
Build row pointers: for i in [0, v52) set v51[i] = this[1] + i * this[12]
Register the row-pointer table with the subsystem: sub_511F23(v57, v51)
Paletted path: when this[0] == 41, read the colour/alpha tables and build the 256-entry RGBA conversion table
Read the 24-bit colour field: if MaskedReadAt8(v57, v56, 8) succeeds, GuardedFieldReader(v57, v56, &v54, &v50) reads the colour source and entry count
Read the alpha/RGB table: if MaskedReadAt8(v57, v56, 16) succeeds, MediaFormatQuery(v57, v56, &v43, &v48, 0) reads the alpha source and entry count

functions.name: DirectXSurfaceFormatNegotiation
functions.summary: Texture format auto-detection and decoding dispatcher. Tries seven image decoders in a fixed priority order (BMP, TGA/generic, DDS-header, unknown sub_50210E, DDS-surface, PPM, DDS-validate) on the raw buffer a2/a3, recording the active candidate in the object at this+0x44/this+0x48 and the caller payload at this+0x40. On the first candidate whose decoder returns a non-negative status it stops; on failure it frees buffers and surface nodes owned by this, resets ownership flags, and retries the next candidate. After success it optionally fills an output descriptor a4 (width/height/depth/FourCC/format/surface-count from this+0xC..this+0x48) and finalizes the linked surface list rooted at this+0x4C/this+0x50. Returns 0 on success, -2005529767 when all candidates fail.

Each iteration records the caller payload a5 at this+0x40, the candidate index at this+0x48, and the constant format code 3 at this+0x44.
Candidate 0: validate BMP header via BMPHeaderValidation(this, a2, a3).
Candidate 1: decompress image texture via ImageTextureDecompressor(this, a2, a3).
Candidate 2: parse DDS header via DDSHeaderParsing(this, a2, a3).
Candidate 3: call the unnamed decoder sub_50210E(this, a2, a3).
Candidate 4: create the DDS texture surface via DDSTextureSurfaceCreation(this, a2, a3).
Candidate 5: decode the PPM P6 image via PPMP6ImageDecoder(this, a2, a3).
Candidate 6: validate/decoding via DDSTextureFormatValidationDecoding(this, a2, a3).
Store the selected decoder's return value as the candidate status v5.
If the candidate status v5 is >= 0, the decode succeeded and the retry loop is exited.
On failure, if the buffer-1 pointer this+0x4 and its ownership flag this+0x38 are both set, free buffer 1 via FreeWrapper_7bcf; likewise free buffer 2 when this+0x8 and this+0x3C are set.
On failure, release the surface head node this+0x4C and the next-surface pointer this+0x50 via ShortComputation_0fae(node, 1) when each is non-null.
Reset decoder state for the next candidate: zero this+0x4, this+0x8, this+0x38, this+0x3C, this+0x4C and this+0x50, then increment the candidate counter v22.
If all seven candidates failed (v22 == 7), return -2005529767.
If the output descriptor a4 is non-null, populate it from the decoded object.
Derive the output FourCC code from this+0x0 via FourCCDecoder.

Zero the 0x1C-byte output descriptor a4, then fill width from this+0xC, height from this+0x10, depth from this+0x14, base surface count 1, format from this+0x44 and the candidate index from this+0x48.
Count the surfaces in the linked list rooted at this+0x4C by walking each node's next pointer (node+0x4C) and incrementing the surface count a4[3].

Finalize each surface node in the chain: copy node+0xC to node+0x20 and node+0x10 to node+0x24, save node+0x14 into node+0x2C, zero node+0x18, node+0x1C and node+0x28, then advance through node+0x4C and to the next surface at this+0x50.
Return 0 after successful decode and surface finalization.

functions.name: DirectXVertexBufferFormatConversion
functions.summary: Converts per-vertex float data between normalized, signed, and direct coordinate ranges based on a destination format code this[2] and a source format code this[1042]. Reads 4 floats per element from a2 + 8 with a 16-byte stride, applies the (dest, source) conversion to each channel, writes the results to this[1043], and returns the output pointer this[1043]. Unhandled format combinations fall through without writing.

operations.description: Dispatch on the destination format selector this[2] via a switch with cases 1, 2 and 3.

Within each destination case, dispatch on the source format selector this[1042]: case 1 accepts source 2 or 3, case 2 accepts source 1 or 3, case 3 accepts source 1 or 2; unmatched source combinations fall through.

Iterate over this[1046] elements; read 4 input floats per element starting at a2 + 8, advance the input pointer by 16 bytes (4 dwords) each iteration, and write the converted values into the output region at this[1043].

Destination format 1: map each channel from signed range to normalized range via (v + 1.0) * 0.5; the alpha channel is passed through unchanged when source format is 2, and also scaled when source format is 3.

Destination format 2: map each channel from normalized range to signed range via v * 2.0 - 1.0; the alpha channel is passed through unchanged when source format is 1, and mapped via (v + 1.0) * 0.5 when source format is 3.
Destination format 3: for source format 1 all four channels are mapped via v * 2.0 - 1.0; for source format 2 the RGB channels pass through unchanged and the alpha channel is mapped via v + v - 1.0.
Return the output pointer this[1043].
